Two measurements are paired when the design supplies a defensible link between them. In translation research, the link may be an aligned passage rather than a speaker. We call this link the **alignment unit** (AU): the unit that must remain intact whenever the two language measurements are compared.

## UCCA graphs across translation

We use the public CC BY-SA 3.0 [English](https://github.com/UniversalConceptualCognitiveAnnotation/UCCA_English-20K) and [French](https://github.com/UniversalConceptualCognitiveAnnotation/UCCA_French-20K) UCCA 20K v2 corpora. Sulem, Abend, and Rappoport ([2015](https://aclanthology.org/W15-3502/)) ask whether UCCA structure is preserved across translations; the same bilingual annotator annotated the two languages separately. Current UCCA guidelines are described by Abend et al. ([2020](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.15810)).

UCCA is a graph representation. A distinct **Scene** is a foundational node with an outgoing Process (`P`) or State (`S`) edge. A remote edge points to an already represented unit and does not create another Scene. One row in the extract is one language side of a passage graph; the analysis unit is one of the 154 source-order English--French passage pairs.

The current v2 release is not the numerical release reported in the 2015 paper. The paper reports 583 sentences per language and mean Scene counts of 9.49 in English and 9.25 in French. <!-- dqr-allow: reference-metadata --> The pinned v2 graphs form the aligned passage pairs loaded below and produce different graph-derived counts. We apply the paper's paired estimand to v2; we do not claim to reproduce the paper's numbers.

```{r}
#| label: load-ucca-pairs
library(ggplot2)

ucca <- read.csv(
  "data/ucca-french-english/passage-counts.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
english <- ucca[ucca$language == "en", ]
french <- ucca[ucca$language == "fr", ]
english <- english[order(english$pair_id), ]
french <- french[order(french$pair_id), ]

stopifnot(
  identical(english$pair_id, french$pair_id),
  nrow(english) == 154L,
  sum(english$scene_count) == 1839L,
  sum(french$scene_count) == 2121L
)

pairs <- data.frame(
  pair_id = english$pair_id,
  chapter = english$chapter,
  english_scenes = english$scene_count,
  french_scenes = french$scene_count,
  english_terminals = english$terminal_count,
  french_terminals = french$terminal_count
)
pairs$difference <- pairs$french_scenes - pairs$english_scenes
```

## Pairing changes the variance

For pair $i$, define $D_i=Y_{i,\mathrm{fr}}-Y_{i,\mathrm{en}}$. Then

$$
\overline D=\overline Y_{\mathrm{fr}}-\overline Y_{\mathrm{en}}
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{Var}[D]
=\operatorname{Var}[Y_{\mathrm{fr}}]
+\operatorname{Var}[Y_{\mathrm{en}}]
-2\operatorname{Cov}(Y_{\mathrm{fr}},Y_{\mathrm{en}}).
$$

Positive covariance can make paired differences substantially less variable than a comparison that discards alignment.

```{r}
#| label: summarize-ucca-pairs
pair_summary <- data.frame(
  pairs = nrow(pairs),
  mean_english_scenes = mean(pairs$english_scenes),
  mean_french_scenes = mean(pairs$french_scenes),
  mean_signed_difference = mean(pairs$difference),
  covariance = cov(pairs$english_scenes, pairs$french_scenes),
  correlation = cor(pairs$english_scenes, pairs$french_scenes)
)
pair_summary
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-ucca-pairs
#| fig-cap: "Graph-derived Scene counts in aligned v2 passages. The identity line marks exact count agreement."
limits <- range(c(pairs$english_scenes, pairs$french_scenes))

ggplot(pairs, aes(english_scenes, french_scenes)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "grey55", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(color = "grey25", size = 1.6, alpha = 0.65) + # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting
  coord_equal(xlim = limits, ylim = limits) +
  labs(x = "Scenes in English passage", y = "Scenes in French passage") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
```

The count correlation is `r sprintf("%.3f", pair_summary$correlation)`, but correlation does not establish agreement. Points can follow a line closely while remaining systematically above the identity line. The next page thus uses an absolute count-agreement target.

The AU must be preserved: v2 filenames are internal annotation identifiers, not bilingual order. The prepared table reconstructs source order from passage ranges and repository history. Sorting filenames would invent pairs.

## Check your understanding

1. What is the observational unit for the paired analysis?
2. Why does a remote edge not create another Scene?
3. How does covariance enter the variance of a difference?
4. Why is a high correlation insufficient evidence of count agreement?

<details class="understanding-answers">
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. One aligned English--French passage pair is the observational unit. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
2. A remote edge points to a unit already represented in the graph; it does not introduce a new Process or State unit and thus does not create a new Scene. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
3. $\operatorname{Var}[D]=\operatorname{Var}[Y_{\mathrm{fr}}]+\operatorname{Var}[Y_{\mathrm{en}}]-2\operatorname{Cov}(Y_{\mathrm{fr}},Y_{\mathrm{en}})$, so positive covariance reduces difference variance. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
4. Correlation measures co-movement, not equality; points can track a line closely while lying systematically above the identity line. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->

</details>
